front.title: Service Orchestration with YANG-modeled Abstractions Framework

abstract.t: This document defines the Service Orchestration with YANG-modeled Abstractions Framework (SOYA) for building layered orchestration systems using YANG models, and specifies the interactions between different orchestration layers.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The YANG Data Modeling Language () has become ubiquitous in modern network management and is widely adopted for modeling configuration and state data for network devices. YANG equally lends itself to describing higher-level orchestration intent at various layers of abstraction.

This document defines the Service Orchestration with YANG-modeled Abstractions (SOYA) Framework for building layered orchestration systems. Each layer allows for the expression of a service intent, according to a set of YANG models. These layers may be hosted on separate SOYA Orchestrators or within a single SOYA Orchestrator, depending on the deployment architecture.

Service intent, e.g. configuration, flows from the highest abstraction layer down to the managed devices. Operational state, on the other hand, flows from the devices up to the higher abstraction layers. The framework specifies permissible data exchanges between different abstraction layers, both within a single SOYA Orchestrator and across multiple SOYA Orchestrators.

section.name: Definition of SOYA Orchestrator
section.t: In the context of this document, a SOYA Orchestrator refers to a software component responsible for managing network services by processing service intent and operational state. Network orchestrators, network controllers, and other similar components are collectively referred to as "SOYA Orchestrators".

section.name: The SOYA Orchestrator
section.t: A SOYA Orchestrator is a software component capable of receiving, storing, and processing service intent. In a SOYA Orchestrator, intent is stored in a datastore as defined in RFC 7950. SOYA Orchestrators must implement, at a minimum, the running-config datastore as defined in .

Processing each received intent update involves executing the SOYA Orchestrator's business logic. Typically, this will result in a corresponding output intent for next orchestration layer down; or for the managed device(s) in case of the lowest service layer.

The SOYA Orchestrator may also support receiving/collecting operational state from its managed devices or from the service layer below. Upon receiving operational state updates, the SOYA Orchestrator SHOULD persist them in its datastore. Processing each received operational state update involves analyzing it according to its business logic and determining the necessary actions. Those may include updating the SOYA Orchestrator's internal state, generating new service intents for the lower layer, or triggering specific configuration changes on managed devices. The SOYA Orchestrator can also propagate operational state updates to the next orchestration layer up. The SOYA Orchestrator can also generate notifications or raise alarms.

section.name: Single-Layer Orchestrator
section.t: A single-layer SOYA Orchestrator is responsible for managing network services at a specific layer of abstraction. It processes service intents and operational state relevant to its layer and interacts with both the higher orchestration layer (if any) and the lower orchestration layer or managed devices.

section.name: Multi-Layer Orchestrator
section.t: A multi-layer SOYA Orchestrator is capable of managing network services on multiple layers of abstraction within a single SOYA Orchestrator.

section.name: Service Layering
section.t: An overall orchestration system may be comprised of multiple layers, each responsible for a specific level of abstraction in managing network services. The schema for each layer is defined by a set of YANG models.
